svg.textArea:
1. The grand-total chains are hardcoded row lists — and they disagree with each other. O1 and the six daily equivalents (AI1, AN1, AS1, AX1, BC1, BH1) are each a hand-typed chain of ~65 cell references. They should be identical apart from the column letter. They are not: O1 includes O201, while AI1 and all five other day columns skip row 201. O1 omits row 238; all six day columns include it. All seven chains list "…+192+187+…" — row 187 out of sequence, suggesting later hand-patching.
So "Total Breadline Bags" differs in composition depending which column you read, and at least two dough groups are silently dropped from one total or another. Any new dough group is missing from all 14 chains until someone edits each by hand. Replacing these with SUMIF on column D ("Breadline" / "MCS LINE") would make them self-maintaining and eliminate the whole bug class.
2. Rows 532-646 are broken. ~115 rows of staging returning #N/A (K, U), #VALUE! (N, O — rows 534-537, Philly Dough) and #REF! (N538, O538 — Bahn Mi Dough). New items part-way through being wired up. They sit below the total chains so printed numbers are safe, but they recalculate on every change and make the sheet look broken.
3. Column A is abandoned and partly broken. A3 reads "Need to Fix This Formula". Only 9 formula cells remain, and A198 is =ROUNDUP((#REF!*2880)/140,0) — a hard broken reference. The 2880 and 130/140 divisors are unexplained magic numbers with no labelled source cell.
4. Column E propagates batch lbs by chained relative reference. Header rows compute the SUMIF correctly; item rows are =E6 — but 33 cells in rows 66-255 are =E$65, pointing at one fixed row. If those were meant to follow each group's own header, they are using the wrong batch size. Worth spot-checking.
5. Seven manual daily maintenance points on this tab alone. E1, F1, K1, G1 carry "don't delete / manually adjust" warnings; K3, L3, O3 say "Adjust this formula daily". The six pre-built day blocks (AD:BH) look designed to eliminate exactly this, but the main K:O block is still what gets printed — so the daily formula-editing ritual continues. Pointing K/L at the right day block via CHOOSE/INDEX on a weekday index would retire most of it.
6. O is a soft link that has already drifted. O defaults to =N, but overrides overwrite the formula. Cells like =O158*1 show ad-hoc patching. Once someone overrides, there is no record of what the optimal figure was, so plan-vs-optimal variance cannot be reviewed. A separate override column beside N would preserve both.
7. Type inconsistency persists. K, AD and others return text "0" rather than numeric 0 — the same issue flagged on DoughWeights and the Schedule Templates. SUM skips text, so any future total over these columns would undercount.
8. U470 and U466 show #DIV/0! — ROUNDUP(K/J,0) where J is blank on dough-header and spacer rows. Cosmetic, but it appears inside the Slice Sheet print zone.
9. Phantom used range. getUsedRange reports A1:AAE646 (707 columns) but real content stops at BN (66 columns). Clearing the unused columns would cut file size and make navigation far less painful.

tr.td: Two JM sub-roll items off Open Sales Lines
Scratch / staging - new items not yet wired

foreignObject.data-title: Planned bags and mixer hours per day

svg.foreignObject:
# Mix-Slice-Oven Sheet — Logic Spec
**Purpose:** The conversion hub. It takes unit shortfalls from Daily Supply & Demand and dough pounds from DoughWeights, converts them into bags to mix, rounds them up to whole mixes, calculates mixer minutes, then splits the output into three printable sheets for three different teams (Mix / Slice / Oven).
**One-line summary:** Units needed → dough lbs ÷ batch size = raw bags → round up to whole mixes = planned bags → ÷ bags-per-mix × run-time = mixer hours.
**Why it matters:** This is where the "raw → optimal → planned" three-stage rounding happens, and where the two production lines get separated. Every number the schedulers actually act on originates here.
## 0. Real extent vs. phantom extent
`getUsedRange` reports A1:AAE646 (707 columns) — that is phantom formatting. Actual content lives only in **A:BN** (66 columns), plus a few stray cells in W:AC.
## 1. Row grouping — dough header + its items
Within rows 6-469 the data repeats in small blocks:
``` row 6 DOUGH HEADER H6 = D10014 (dough code), I6 = "Sour Dough" E6 = batch lbs, N6/O6 = SUM(N7:N19)/SUM(O7:O19) rows 7-19 ITEM ROWS each finished product made from that dough ```
Item rows come in **pack-code / case-code pairs** (F3005 / F53005) — the F5xxxx case row carries J=1 and usually resolves to 0.
The **Breadline/MCS split at row ~258** is the single most important structural fact. Every grand-total formula is a hardcoded chain of row references, hand-split at that boundary: row 1 formulas sum the Breadline rows, row 2 formulas sum the MCS rows.
## 2. Band A · Identity & setup (A-J)
| Col | Header | Formula / source | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | A | PANS | `=ROUNDUP((L20*2880)/130,0)` | only 9 cells, rows 20-254. A3 says "Need to Fix This Formula". A198 = `=ROUNDUP((#REF!*2880)/140,0)` — broken. | | B | Sequence on Schedule | `=XLOOKUP($C7,CLI!D:D, CLI!F:F)` | run order, 357 cells | | C | Unique Dough | manual text | join key consumed by both Schedule Templates | | D | Asset | manual — "Breadline" / "MCS LINE" | line assignment | | E | batch lbs | `=SUMIF('DoughWeights'!Z:Z, $H6, 'DoughWeights'!AL:AL)` on header rows; `=E6` on item rows | lbs per batch from the raw BOM dump. E1: "Don't delete this data." | | F | optimal bags per mix | manual — 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4 | drives run-time selection everywhere | | G | Scrap Factor | manual (1.1, blank) | G1: "Manually adjust scrap rate as necessary" | | H | Finished Product# | manual — F3005, D10014 | join key into Daily S&D!E:E and DoughWeights!B:B | | I | Finished Product Description | manual | | | J | Units per case/Tray | manual | divisor for tray counts |
## 3. Band B · The core conversion (K → O) — the heart of the sheet
**K — Number of Individual Packaged Units Needed** (K3: "Adjust this formula daily")
``` =IFERROR(IF(XLOOKUP($H6,'Daily Supply & Demand'!E:E,'Daily Supply & Demand'!V:V)<0, ABS(XLOOKUP($H6,'Daily Supply & Demand'!E:E,'Daily Supply & Demand'!V:V)), "0"),"0") ```
Same negative-shortfall gate used on DoughWeights. 524 cells.
**L — dough lbs → raw bags**
``` =(XLOOKUP($H6,'DoughWeights'!$B:$B,'DoughWeights'!L:L) / $E6) * G6 ```
= (pounds of dough needed ÷ pounds per batch) × scrap factor. 635 cells. **This is the single most important formula in the workbook.**
**M — Bags Needed · Raw Total** — `=SUM(L7:L13)` on header rows (fractional, e.g. 4.37 bags)
**N — Bags Needed · Optimal Total** — the rounding decision
``` =CEILING(SUM(L7:L13), F7) header rows, group of items =CEILING(L53, F53) standalone rows ```
Rounds raw bags up to the nearest whole multiple of F (optimal bags per mix). You cannot mix half a batch — this enforces it. Header roll-up: `=SUM(N7:N19)`.
**O — Bags Needed · Planned Total** — `=N7`, a soft link. O3: *"Adjust this formula daily (reset it and then manually adjust to the # of bags you want mixed)"*
O is the **human override layer**. It defaults to the optimal figure and the scheduler types over it. `O:O` is what both Schedule Templates read.
### The three-stage rounding chain
``` L (raw, fractional) → M (raw sum) → N (CEILING to whole mixes) → O (human override) → PRINTED ```
## 4. Band C · Slice Sheet output (P-V)
P1 banner: *"This section gets printed & distributed to the packaging team (for slicing) and the Oven Sheet Gets Sent to the Oven Team"*
| Col | Header | Formula | |---|---|---| | P | Dough | `=C7` | | Q | # of Bags for Mixing | `=O7` | | R | Finished Product# | `=H7` | | S | Product Description | `=I7` | | T | # of Individual Packs/Cases Needed | `=K7` | | U | # of Trays/Cases Needed | `=ROUNDUP(K7/J7,0)` | | V | Tray/Case | manual |
Pure re-presentation — no new logic. Q3 = `TODAY()`, R3 = `TEXT(Q3,"dddd")`.
## 5. Band D · Grand totals (rows 1-5)
| Cell | Value | Formula | |---|---|---| | N1/O1 | Total Breadline Bags = 131.5 | hardcoded chain `=O7+O14+O21+…+O257` (65 terms) | | N2/O2 | Total MCS Bags = 229 | hardcoded chain `=O264+O267+…+O469` (63 terms) | | S2/T2 | Grand Total of Bags to Mix = 360.5 | `=O1+O2` |
O1 and O2 are the two cells the Schedule Templates read into their H2 header (O1 → Breadline, O2 → MCS).
## 6. Band E · Six day blocks (AD-BH)
K1 banner: *"This is the section where you plan the total number of bags per mix for each day's mixing schedule"*
**AD is shared across all days** — Run Time Per Mix (min), the same IFS on `$F` that both Schedule Templates use:
``` =IFS($F6=1, XLOOKUP($C6,CLI!$D:$D,CLI!$J:$J), $F6=2, …CLI!$I:$I, $F6=3, …CLI!$H:$H, $F6=4, …CLI!$G:$G, $F6=1.5, …CLI!$K:$K, $F6=0, "0") ```
Then six identical 5-column blocks, each replicating K/L/M/N/O for one weekday. Each block's row 1 / row 2 carry that day's Breadline / MCS bag totals — **these 12 cells are exactly what Daily Supply & Demand pulls back into rows 1-4 of each wrap sheet, closing the loop.**
## 7. Band F · Mixer hours (BI-BN) — the capacity check
``` BI6 = IFERROR((AI6/$F6)*$AD6, 0) Sunday BJ6 → AN6 (Mon) · BK6 → AS6 (Tue) · BL6 → AX6 (Wed) · BM6 → BC6 (Thu) · BN6 → BH6 (Fri) ```
= (planned bags ÷ bags per mix) × minutes per mix = minutes on the mixer. Row 1 / row 2 total them and convert to hours (÷60).
These are the **reality check** — ~24 hrs on a mixer per day means the plan is at or past capacity. Also fed back to Daily Supply & Demand rows 1-4.
## 8. Band G · Oven Sheet (rows 471-529)
B471 = "Oven Sheet", A472 = "PANS". Reuses columns with **different meanings**:
| Col | Meaning here | |---|---| | D | Product group name | | G | `=XLOOKUP($D473,C:C,O:O)` — pulls planned bags back by group name | | J | Trays per 1 Bag Mix | | N | Pieces Per pan (not "bags needed") | | O | Scrap factor (not "planned bags") | | U | # of Pans/Boxes to set out | | V | Notes/Comments |
U uses three different formulas depending on row: `=ROUNDUP(K/J,0)`, `=ROUNDUP(K/N,0)`, `=ROUNDUP(((K473*M473)+(K474*M474))/N473,0)`.
## Verification scope
Read A1:V6 and AD1:BN6 in full detail, ran a complete formula-pattern scan of A1:V646 (top 4 patterns per column with row ranges and counts), mapped populated columns across A1:ZD646, and read value detail for rows 466-546. Not every one of the ~470 item rows was read individually, and the ~65 terms in all 14 total chains were not each verified against the actual dough-group header rows — the chains were compared against each other, which is how the row 201 / row 238 discrepancies surfaced. No changes were made to the workbook.
